title: census.today, kbdecide, provider and kg_history date a run by the local day while factdiff.today names the UTC day
goal: census.today() and the other local-date defaults (kbdecide._today, provider probed_utc, kg_history --date check) name the same day at any hour in any time zone, the UTC day factdiff.today() names, so a census date and the factdiff logs and stamps of one run do not differ by a day

run: import os,time,sys;sys.path.insert(0,'_tools');import census,kbdecide,factdiff;d=[];[(os.environ.__setitem__('TZ',z),time.tzset(),d.append((census.today(),kbdecide.day(None),factdiff.today()))) for z in ('Etc/GMT-14','Etc/GMT+12')];print(d);sys.exit(0 if len({x for t in d for x in t})==1 else 1)

notes: SP-wjp5qllo review (S3) found it again: census.today() (census.py:265) and kbdecide.py:294 are still the local day, and census run passes --date to factdiff detect and apply, so a census in the window dates verified_utc and confirmed one day off from the UTC checked_utc stamps. Premise (2026-10-14, ae319c43c5): census.today() under TZ Etc/GMT-14 vs Etc/GMT+12 gives two days, exit 1; kbdecide.day(None) (the goal's kbdecide._today is the function day; kblog.py imports it) and provider.probed_utc and kg_history's future-date check use the local day too; factdiff.today() is UTC. The repro now compares census, kbdecide and factdiff in the two extreme zones. One helper in kbcommon.py (factdiff imports provider, so provider cannot import factdiff). Test: a TZ assertion in a census helper of test_redact.py's test_census_queue_and_census_groups id, TZ restored with time.tzset; no new id. Planning 2026-10-14: the test-selection checks pass before the work by design: they pin behaviour that must stay, and the work extends the named test function with the new assertions (no new test id); the other checks fail on the premise.
